newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria ends troubled steel mill contract - agency.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria ends troubled steel mill contract - agency.

text.p: Nigeria's military government has terminated a contract with Russian firm Tiajpromexport (TPE) for construction of the troubled $5 billion Ajaokuta steel mill, the national news agency said on Thursday.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) quoted sources at the mill as saying TPE had been paid 50 billion naira ($625 million) at the end of 1996 to terminate the contract which is estimated to have cost $5 billion.
Russia began construction of the steel mill in 1979 but Nigeria's failure to pay its debts has stalled completion, which the power and steel ministry says has reached 98 percent.
NAN said TPE would be on standby for jobs on the mill, which would be charged as they were carried out.
The Ajaokuta Steel Complex is one of four steel rolling mills ordered by a government awash with oil money in the 1970s, to reduce imports and use Nigerian iron ore.
The World Bank carried out a study on the complex between 1990 and 1991 and advised government to stop the project, saying it was too capital-intensive.
The present military government says it is committed to completing Ajaokuta.
